newsitem.title: CHINA: China share-issuing firms to keep interest on bids.
newsitem.headline: China share-issuing firms to keep interest on bids.

text.p: Chinese companies that issue shares will be allowed to retain interest income on funds from investors bidding for shares, even if the bids are unsuccessful, the official newspaper China Securities said on Saturday.

Income from the face and surplus value of issued shares along with the interest income from funds used for successful bids would be accounted for in the accumulated capital of enterprises after issue costs were deducted, the paper said.
Interest on funds frozen during unsuccessful bids would also belong to the share-issuing enterprise and not to the would-be investor, it quoted new Ministry of Finance regulations as saying.
Such income would be accounted for in extra-management funds if the amount was relatively small and in five-year average turnover if it was relatively big, it said.
Enterprises would be required to make clear the source of the income in their annual reports, the newspaper said but gave no details.
